Responsible Tourism Guidelines
Experience Odisha, Sustain Its Legacy

Odisha is a land of pristine beaches, ancient temples, dense mangrove forests, and vibrant tribal cultures. As we open our doors to the world, we invite you to be a partner in preserving this beauty. Responsible tourism isn't just a choice; it's a shared commitment to protect what makes Odisha unique.

TRAVEL WITH PURPOSE
Respect the Environment

Say No to Plastic: Single-use plastics are banned in many heritage zones and national parks. Carry a reusable water bottle and bag.

Save Water & Energy: Practice conservation in hotels. Turn off lights/AC when leaving and reuse towels if possible.

Leave No Trace: Dispose of waste only in designated bins. If you can't find one, carry your trash back with you.

Honor Our Heritage

Dress Modestly: Cover shoulders and knees when visiting temples like Jagannath Puri or Lingaraj. Remove footwear where required.

Protect Monuments: Do not touch intricate carvings or scribble on walls at sites like Konark or Udayagiri caves.

Photography Etiquette: Always ask for permission before photographing people, especially in tribal areas. Respect 'No Photography' zones.

Support Local Communities

Buy Local: Purchase sarees (Sambalpuri, Bomkai) and handicrafts (Pattachitra) directly from artisans or government emporiums.

Eat Local: Try authentic Odia cuisine at local restaurants. It supports the local economy and reduces food miles.

No Child Labor: Do not employ children as guides or buy from them. Report such instances to the Child Helpline (1098).

Wildlife Etiquette

Odisha is home to diverse wildlife sanctuaries like Similipal and Bhitarkanika. Helping us keep them wild is crucial.

Maintain Silence

Loud noises disturb animals. Keep designated routes and maintain silence during safaris.

No Feeding

Feeding wild animals alters their natural diet and behavior, leading to potential conflict.

Wear Earth Tones

Bright colors can startle animals. Wear greens, browns, or beige during nature walks.

Tribal Sensitivity

Odisha has 62 distinct tribes. Interactions should be respectful, dignified, and non-intrusive.

Seek Permission

Always visit tribal areas with an authorized guide who understands the local dialect and customs.

No Aggressive Photography

Treat people with dignity. Do not treat tribal markets as photo-ops without consent.

Responsible Gifting

Avoid giving money or sweets to children. Instead, donate to local schools or NGOs if you wish to help.

TRAVEL ADVISORY
Safety Advisories

Odisha welcomes you with its rich heritage, vibrant culture, and diverse natural landscapes. To ensure a safe and enjoyable travel experience, visitors are advised to follow the safety guidelines outlined below and remain aware of local conditions during their journey.

Stay Informed, Stay Prepared
Keep yourself updated with official travel advisories, weather alerts, and local guidelines.
Register your travel plans with your accommodation or tour operator when visiting remote areas.
Save important contacts, including local authorities and hotel details, for quick access.
General Safety Guidelines
Carry valid photo identification at all times (physical and digital copies).
Avoid carrying large amounts of cash; use digital payments where possible.
Stay alert in crowded places such as markets, festivals, and transport hubs.
Use only authorized taxis, registered guides, and verified tour operators.
Do not accept food or beverages from strangers.
Health & Well-being
Drink only bottled or purified water.
Prefer freshly cooked food from hygienic establishments.
Carry essential medications and prescriptions.
Use sunscreen, hats, and stay hydrated, especially during summer months.
In case of illness, visit the nearest government or accredited private hospital.
Women Travellers
Odisha is widely regarded as a safe destination; however, standard precautions are recommended:
Avoid isolated areas and late-night travel alone.
Choose reputable accommodations and transport services.
Share your itinerary with a trusted contact.
Trust your instincts and seek help if you feel uncomfortable.
Beach & Coastal Safety
Swim only in designated areas under lifeguard supervision (especially at Puri, Chandrabhaga, and Gopalpur beaches).
Strictly follow flag warnings and safety signage.
Avoid swimming during high tide, rough sea, or cyclone alerts.
Do not venture too deep into the sea; currents can be strong and unpredictable.
Refrain from alcohol consumption before entering the water.
Wildlife & Eco-Tourism Safety
Follow instructions from forest officials and certified guides at all times.
Maintain a safe distance from wildlife, including crocodiles and dolphins.
Do not feed animals or attempt close interaction.
Wear appropriate clothing and footwear for forest and trekking areas.
Avoid littering and respect eco-sensitive zones.
Monsoon, Cyclones & Weather Advisory
Odisha’s coastal regions may experience cyclones and heavy rainfall, particularly between June and November.
Monitor weather updates from official sources before and during travel.
Avoid sea activities and coastal travel during warnings.
Follow evacuation or safety instructions issued by local authorities.
Temple & Cultural Etiquette
Follow dress codes and entry guidelines at religious sites.
Photography may be restricted in certain temples (e.g., inside sanctums).
Remove footwear before entering temple premises.
Respect rituals, queues, and local customs.
Beware of unauthorized intermediaries offering services.
Transport & Road Safety
Use registered vehicles and licensed drivers.
Wear seatbelts and helmets where applicable.
Avoid night travel in unfamiliar or remote areas.
Be cautious while driving on rural or forest roads.
Digital & Financial Safety
Use secure payment methods and avoid public Wi-Fi for financial transactions.
Verify booking websites before making payments.
Keep emergency backup funds and cards.
PRIORITY ACCESS
Emergency Assistance
Police: 100 / 112
Ambulance: 108
Fire Services: 101
Tourist Helpline: 1800-11-1363
For immediate assistance, contact your nearest police station or tourism information centre.
Responsible & Sustainable Travel
Preserve Odisha’s natural and cultural heritage.
Avoid single-use plastics and dispose of waste responsibly.
Support local communities, artisans, and eco-friendly initiatives.
Be a respectful and mindful traveller.
Disclaimer

Travel conditions may vary due to weather, local events, or unforeseen circumstances. Visitors are advised to follow instructions from local authorities and rely on official government communication channels for the latest updates.

ILLUMINATING THE HISTORY OF ODISHA
/

Light & Sound Shows
DHAULI
KONARK
Dhauli Light & Sound Show

"Where a war changed the course of humanity."

Brief History

Perched on the serene Dhauli Hills overlooking the Daya River, the Dhauli Shanti Stupa stands close to the site of the historic Kalinga War fought in 261 BCE. It was here that Emperor Ashoka witnessed the devastation of war and embraced the path of peace and Buddhism, transforming from the feared "Chandashoka" to the compassionate "Dharmashoka".

About the Show

The Dhauli Light & Sound Show is a spectacular 35-minute 3D projection mapping experience that transforms the white Peace Pagoda into a living canvas of history. Through immersive visuals, dramatic narration and music, the show retells the story of the Kalinga War, Ashoka's remorse, and the rise of Buddhism from the land of Odisha.

Set against the tranquil backdrop of the Daya River, the experience combines history, spirituality and cutting-edge technology in a deeply moving evening attraction.

Important Information
LOCATION
Dhauli Shanti Stupa, Bhubaneswar
DURATION
Approx. 35 minutes
SHOW TIMINGS
Hindi: Around 7:00 PM | English: Around 7:30 PM (Timings may vary seasonally)
TICKET PRICE
Approx. ₹100 for adults | ₹50 for students
LANGUAGES
Hindi, English & Odia
BOOK ONLINE 

Tickets also available at venue

 Tip: Arrive early for the best seating and evening views of the illuminated stupa. Closed on Mondays.

SUSTAINABLE ADVENTURE TOURISM
Welcome to Mahendragiri Eco-Adventure Fest 2026

Mahendragiri, the second-highest peak in Odisha, rises majestically from the Eastern Ghats, offering a pristine natural landscape rich in biodiversity and cultural heritage. The Mahendragiri Eco-Adventure Fest 2026 brings this remarkable destination to life through a unique celebration of adventure, ecology, and community.

About the Fest

The Mahendragiri Eco-Adventure Fest is designed to promote sustainable adventure tourism in Odisha while showcasing the ecological importance of the region. The festival brings together adventure sports, environmental awareness, and community engagement, encouraging responsible tourism and eco-sensitive practices.

It also creates opportunities for visitors to interact with local communities while exploring the natural and cultural richness of Mahendragiri.

Show more 
Event Details
VENUE
Mahendragiri Hills, Gajapati District, Odisha
DATES
25 April – 26 April 2026
THEME
Ecology & Adventure
ENGAGEMENT
Community & Sports
ENTRY
Free (Activity-based charges applicable)
REGISTER & PARTICIPATE 
WHY ATTEND
Why You Should Attend
ECO-ADVENTURE

Experience Odisha’s premier eco-adventure festival

COMMUNITY

Participate alongside athletes and adventure enthusiasts

UNTOUCHED NATURE

Explore untouched natural landscapes

LOCAL CULTURE

Engage with local culture and traditions

SUSTAINABILITY

Be part of sustainable tourism initiatives

ESSENTIAL GUIDE
Plan Your Visit
Getting There

Mahendragiri can be reached via Koinpur village (base location) and Paralakhemundi (district hub). The nearest airport is Visakhapatnam (4–5 hrs), followed by Bhubaneswar (7–8 hrs). Rail access is available via Palasa (1–2 hrs) and Paralakhemundi stations (1.5–2 hrs). Well-connected roads from Paralakhemundi, Brahmapur, and Visakhapatnam offer scenic hill routes to the festival site.

Accommodation & Logistics

Basic stay options are available at Koinpur village, including lodges and homestays, while Paralakhemundi offers hotels and guesthouses. Camping facilities will also be arranged near the festival area. Participants in paid competitions will be provided basic accommodation and meals, while other visitors are required to arrange their own stay and travel.

Responsible Tourism

Visitors are encouraged to follow eco-friendly practices, avoid littering, and respect local culture and traditions. Adhering to safety and environmental guidelines will help preserve the natural beauty of Mahendragiri and ensure a sustainable experience.

A JOURNEY OF FAITH WHERE THE GODS COME AMONG THE PEOPLE
The Divine Journey of Ratha Jatra

In a world that rarely slows down, Ratha Jatra in Puri offers a rare moment of pause, joy, and shared celebration. Once every year, Lord Jagannath, along with his brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra, leaves the sanctum of the Shree Mandir and comes out onto the streets of Puri to meet his devotees. From the Ratnasinghasan, the Lord is carried by his Sevayats in the ceremonial procession known as Pahandi, swaying gracefully to the rhythm of brass gongs, cymbals, conches, and devotional chants as waves of faith fill the air.

This is not a festival you merely witness, you become part of it. People pull the chariots together, walk alongside the deities, and chant with strangers who feel like family for the day. The towering wooden chariots move slowly through Bada Danda, the Grand Road of Puri, transforming the city into a river of devotion.

The story begins after Deba Snana Purnima, when the deities are believed to fall ill following their ceremonial bath. They rest in seclusion for a few days, cared for like members of a family. Once they recover, they set out for their annual journey to the Gundicha Temple, believed to be their aunt’s home. The journey feels deeply familiar and human, a homecoming filled with affection, celebration, and togetherness.

Along the way, the chariots make a symbolic halt near the samadhi of Salabega, the revered Odia poet-devotee of Lord Jagannath. Born to a Muslim father and a Hindu mother, Salabega’s timeless bhajans remain deeply woven into Jagannath culture. Tradition holds that the Lord pauses here to honour the devotion of his beloved devotee, making the moment one of the most moving expressions of inclusivity and compassion within the festival.

Ratha Jatra resonates with anyone who values family, community, and traditions that continue to feel alive across generations.

Show more 
Ratha Jatra 2026
VENUE
Puri, Odisha
DATES
Begins 16 July 2026
What Makes Ratha Jatra So Special?

Every aspect of the festival reflects Odisha’s deep-rooted spiritual and artistic traditions. The three grand chariots — Nandighosha (Lord Jagannath), Taladhwaja (Lord Balabhadra), and Darpadalana (Goddess Subhadra) rise nearly 45 feet high and are freshly handcrafted every year by traditional artisans.

To pull the ropes of the chariots is considered an act of immense spiritual merit and blessing.

Rituals That Tell a Story
PAHANDI BIJE

Before the journey begins, the deities are ceremonially carried out of the temple in a rhythmic, swaying procession accompanied by gongs, cymbals, conches, and chants called Pahandi. It is one of the most emotional moments of the festival.

CHHERA PAHANRA

In a profound gesture of humility, the Gajapati Maharaja of Puri regarded as the foremost servitor of Lord Jagannath sweeps the chariot platforms with a golden broom. The ritual symbolises equality before the divine.

GUNDICHA JATRA

The deities travel to the Gundicha Temple, where they stay for seven days before returning to the main temple. The return journey is known as Bahuda Jatra.

SUNA BESHA

A day after Bahuda Jatra, the deities appear adorned in magnificent golden attire and ornaments weighing over 200 kilograms. This dazzling ritual is known as Suna Besha.

NILADRI BIJE

The concluding ritual carries a gentle, playful charm. As Lord Jagannath returns to the temple, Goddess Lakshmi expresses her displeasure at being left behind. The Lord offers her rasagola as reconciliation, bringing the festival to a sweet and symbolic close.

Dates are based on the traditional Odia Hindu calendar.

Where the Divine Leads, Discovery Follows

While visiting Puri during Ratha Jatra, explore some of Odisha’s most iconic destinations nearby.

Konark Sun Temple
Located about 35 km from Puri, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is a magnificent 13th-century temple dedicated to the Sun God, celebrated for its intricate stone carvings and monumental architecture.
Chilika Lake (Satapada)
A scenic drive from Puri takes you to Asia’s largest brackish water lagoon, home to Irrawaddy dolphins and thousands of migratory birds. A sunrise boat ride here is unforgettable.
Bhubaneswar
Known as the Temple City of India, Bhubaneswar blends ancient heritage with vibrant urban culture. Landmarks such as the Lingaraj Temple stand alongside bustling cafés, markets, and contemporary city life.
What to Try

Whether you are dining at the Temple or at OTDC Panthanivas, or a local eatery, Odisha’s cuisine offers flavours rooted in temple traditions and local culture.

Mahaprasad

The sacred meal of the Jagannath Temple, comprising rice, dal, local vegetables, and desserts prepared without onion or garlic.

Dalma

A wholesome lentil preparation cooked with seasonal vegetables and lightly flavoured with ginger and panch phoran.

Kanika

Aromatic sweet rice prepared with ghee, raisins, and cardamom.

Khata

A tangy relish made from mango, tamarind, or elephant apple.

Kheera Mohan

Known to the world as Rasagola, this iconic Odia sweet has been offered to Lord Jagannath in Puri for centuries and remains deeply woven into the rituals and culinary traditions of the temple.

Chhena Poda

Odisha’s iconic caramelised cheesecake made from fresh chhena and jaggery.

Shop Souvenirs
Pipili

Famous for vibrant appliqué craft including canopies, wall hangings, umbrellas, and lampshades.

Raghurajpur Heritage Village

A heritage crafts village known for Pattachitra paintings, palm leaf engravings, and traditional artisan workshops.

Utkalika

Government-run emporium offering authentic Odisha handlooms, silver filigree, appliqué work, and handicrafts.

Boyanika

A Government run emporium known for curated collections of Sambalpuri textiles, tribal jewellery, and handwoven crafts.

Ekamra Haat

A vibrant urban crafts village showcasing Odisha’s handlooms, handicrafts, and regional cuisine.

When & How to Visit
Dates & Details

WHERE THE SCULPTURES COME ALIVE IN DANCE AND RHYTHM
Timeless Grandeur Under the Starlit Skies

Set against the timeless grandeur of the Konark Sun Temple, the Konark Festival is far more than a celebration of dance and music, it is an experience where heritage comes alive under the starlit skies of a winter night. As evening descends upon Konark and the temple glows in soft golden light, the sculpted dancers carved into its ancient walls seem almost ready to step into motion once again.

Here, art is not confined to stone. It breathes through rhythm, movement, music, and tradition.

Held every year from 1st December to 5th December, the festival transforms Konark into one of India’s most evocative cultural stages, drawing renowned artists, scholars, travellers, and connoisseurs from across the world.

Festival Information
FESTIVAL DATES
1st December – 5th December (Every Year)
VENUE
Open-Air Auditorium, Konark
TIMING
6:00 PM – 8:30 PM
ENTRY TICKET
₹100 per person
About the Festival

Originally envisioned by legendary Odissi maestro Guru Gangadhar Pradhan, the Konark Festival has grown into one of India’s premier classical dance and cultural festivals. Organised by Odisha Tourism in collaboration with cultural institutions, the festival celebrates India’s rich performing arts traditions against the backdrop of one of the country’s greatest architectural masterpieces.

For five magical evenings, internationally acclaimed artists present some of India’s finest classical dance forms including Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, Manipuri, and contemporary classical interpretations.

At the heart of the festival lies Odissi — Odisha’s classical dance tradition deeply inspired by the sculptural elegance of Konark itself. The festival creates a rare dialogue between temple architecture, music, movement, and spirituality, allowing audiences to experience art in one of its most authentic settings.

Together with the International Sand Art Festival at nearby Chandrabhaga Beach, the Konark Festival offers visitors a vibrant cultural journey where heritage, creativity, and coastal beauty converge.

HIGHLIGHTS
What Makes the Konark Festival Special
Performances Against a UNESCO World Heritage Monument

Few cultural festivals in the world unfold before a backdrop as iconic as the Konark Sun Temple. The illuminated temple complex creates a dramatic and unforgettable setting for every performance.

Celebration of India’s Classical Dance Traditions

The festival showcases some of the country’s finest dancers and musicians, representing India’s diverse classical traditions through solo and ensemble performances.

The Spirit of Odissi

Konark and Odissi share a timeless connection. The dance form’s graceful postures and sculptural movements echo the carvings that adorn the temple walls, making the experience deeply rooted in Odisha’s cultural identity.

A Gathering of Art, Heritage and Culture

Beyond performances, the festival attracts cultural enthusiasts, photographers, scholars, and travellers who come together to celebrate India’s living artistic traditions.

VISUAL JOURNEY
Glimpses of Konark Festival
EXPLORE NEARBY
Where Culture Leads, Discovery Follows

While visiting the Konark Festival, explore some of Odisha’s most iconic destinations nearby.

Konark Sun Temple

The 13th-century UNESCO World Heritage Site dedicated to the Sun God remains one of India’s greatest architectural and sculptural achievements.

Chandrabhaga Beach

A scenic beach located near Konark, known for stunning sunrises, serene coastline, and the International Sand Art Festival.

Puri

Home to the Jagannath Temple and the world-famous Ratha Jatra, Puri blends spirituality, beach culture, and vibrant local traditions.

Raghurajpur Heritage Village

A heritage crafts village known for Pattachitra painting, palm leaf engraving, Gotipua dance, and traditional artisan communities.

Bhubaneswar

The Temple City of India offers ancient temples, contemporary urban culture, museums, and excellent Odia cuisine.

What to Try

Experience Odisha’s rich culinary traditions while attending the festival.

Dalma

Lentils cooked with vegetables and traditional spices

Chhena Poda

Odisha’s iconic baked cottage cheese dessert

Coastal Seafood Delicacies

Fresh prawn and fish preparations along the Konark–Puri coast

Shop Souvenirs
Pipili

Famous for colourful appliqué work including lampshades, wall hangings, umbrellas, and textiles.

Raghurajpur Heritage Village

Purchase authentic Pattachitra paintings, palm leaf engravings, masks, and handcrafted souvenirs directly from artisans.

Utkalika

Government-run emporium offering Odisha handicrafts, stone carving, silver filigree, appliqué work, and tribal art.

Boyanika

Government –run emporium known for Sambalpuri sarees, handwoven textiles, tribal jewellery, and curated handloom collections.

Konark Craft Market

Explore local stalls featuring stone sculptures, shell crafts, miniature temple replicas, and handmade décor inspired by Odisha’s artistic traditions.

TRAVEL PLANNING
When & How to Visit
Best Time to Visit

Details: Early December, when Konark hosts both the Konark Festival and the International Sand Art Festival.

How to Reach

Nearest Airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar — approximately 65 km from Konark.

Nearest Railway Stations: Puri and Bhubaneswar.

Travel Tips & Stay

Travel Tip: Plan your journey as part of the Bhubaneswar–Konark–Puri coastal circuit to experience Odisha’s temples, beaches, crafts, cuisine, and cultural festivals together.

Recommended Stay: Konark and nearby Puri offer beach resorts, heritage stays, eco-retreats, and OTDC Panthanivas accommodations suitable for all kinds of travellers.

INCLUSIONS

CELEBRATING THE ARRIVAL OF WINGS FROM ACROSS THE WORLD
National Chilika Bird Festival

Every winter, the skies above Chilika come alive with constant chirping and flapping of wings. From distant Arctic landscapes and Central Asian wetlands, thousands of migratory birds arrive at Odisha’s great lagoon, transforming its waters into one of the most spectacular birding landscapes in Asia. The National Chilika Bird Festival celebrates this extraordinary annual migration and positions Odisha as one of India’s premier birdwatching destinations.

Held at Mangalajodi on the northern fringes of Chilika Lake and Nalabana – the marine bird sanctuary within the lagoon, the festival brings together birders, photographers, conservationists, researchers, nature enthusiasts, and travellers from across India and beyond. It is an invitation to experience the wonder of migration, the richness of wetland biodiversity, and the remarkable conservation story of Chilika.

About the Festival

Organised annually by the Department of Tourism, Government of Odisha, the National Chilika Bird Festival showcases the unparalleled avian diversity of Chilika Lake — Asia’s largest brackish water lagoon and a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance.

Every year during winter, nearly one million migratory birds representing over 200 species arrive at Chilika along the Central Asian Flyway. The festival offers visitors an immersive experience amid vast wetlands filled with calls, whistles, quacks, and wingbeats a living orchestra of migration and survival.

At the heart of the festival lies Mangalajodi, globally recognised as one of India’s finest community-led conservation success stories. Once known for poaching, the village has transformed into a thriving eco-tourism and bird conservation destination, where local communities now serve as protectors and guides to the wetland ecosystem.

The festival aims to promote Odisha as a leading birding and eco-tourism destination while encouraging awareness about wetland conservation, sustainable tourism, and biodiversity protection.

Festival Information
FESTIVAL DATES
Winter Season (November to February)
MAIN VENUE
Mangalajodi & Nalabana, Chilika Lake
ORGANISED BY
Department of Tourism, Government of Odisha
AVIAN PARADISE
Why Chilika Is Special

Stretching across vast expanses of water, marshes, mudflats, reed beds, and islands, Chilika supports an astonishing variety of resident and migratory birdlife. Both Mangalajodi and Nalabana Bird Sanctuary are recognised as Important Bird Areas (IBA), attracting birdwatchers and researchers from around the world.

The unique landscape allows visitors to observe birds at remarkably close range, especially during guided boat safaris through the marsh channels of Mangalajodi.

Visitors can witness:
Massive congregations of ducks, teals, gulls, and waders
Graceful Greater Flamingos, locally known as Hira Pakhi
Black Tailed Godwits, Sandpipers, Avocets, and Ducks
Raptors hunting across open wetlands
Rare and near-threatened species including Grey-headed Lapwing and Greater Painted Snipe
Thousands of Eurasian Wigeons and Northern Shovellers moving in synchronized flocks across the lagoon
FESTIVAL HIGHLIGHT EXPERIENCES
Festival Highlights
Exclusive Visit to Nalabana Bird Sanctuary

One of the festival’s most anticipated experiences is the guided visit to Nalabana Bird Sanctuary — a protected island habitat within Chilika that remains inaccessible to general visitors during most of the year. During the festival, participants can witness nesting colonies, migratory congregations, flamingo gatherings, and pristine wetland habitats rarely accessible to the public.

Guided Birding & Boat Safaris

Expert-led boating experiences through the wetlands offer unparalleled opportunities for birdwatching, photography, and interpretation of migratory behaviour and wetland ecology.

Expert Sessions & Conservation Dialogues

Curated evening interactions bring together ornithologists, conservation practitioners, wildlife photographers, researchers, and birding enthusiasts for engaging discussions on migration, conservation, citizen science, and eco-tourism.

Chilika Boat Festival

Adding a vibrant cultural dimension to the event, the Chilika Boat Festival celebrates the region’s enduring relationship with the lagoon through local traditions, community participation, and lake-based experiences.

VISUAL JOURNEY
Glimpses of Chilika Bird Festival
EXPLORE NEARBY
Where Nature Leads, Discovery Follows

While visiting the National Chilika Bird Festival, explore some of the remarkable destinations around Chilika and coastal Odisha.

Satapada

Famous for Irrawaddy dolphin sightings and scenic boating experiences across the lagoon.

Kalijai Island

A revered island shrine located within Chilika Lake, blending spirituality with stunning natural surroundings.

Barkul & Rambha

Picturesque lakefront destinations ideal for sunrise views, boating, and experiencing the tranquil beauty of Chilika.

Mangalajodi

The heart of the festival and one of India’s most celebrated community-based bird conservation destinations.

TRAVEL PLANNING
When & How to Visit
Dates & Logistics

Best Time to Visit: November to February, when migratory bird activity at Chilika is at its peak.

Connectivity

Nearest Airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar.

Nearest Railway Stations: Balugaon, Khordha Road, Bhubaneswar, and Puri.

Traveler Tips

Travel Tip: Early morning boat safaris at Mangalajodi offer the best opportunities for bird sightings and photography. Carry binoculars, neutral-coloured clothing, and appropriate camera equipment for the best experience.
